Glapinski conference (from 15:00): 'Today all forecasts indicate that the return of inflation to target in Poland is durable'; in Q1 inflation may decline (lower electricity tariffs, cheaper agricultural commodities, disinflation in market goods, slowing services prices -> lower core).

Glapinski on March and terminal rate: asked whether a March cut is possible - 'if our projection does not show anything worrying, nothing suggests it will... and no unexpected external events occur, then in my view the answer is yes'. Feb hold: only three weeks since last meeting, no new inflation data, better activity data - 'nothing fundamentally changed'. In March the MPC will have the Jan flash CPI, wage data and the March projection (incl. effects of 2025 cuts); CPI basket revision mid-March. Inflation assumed broadly on target all year, close to 2.5%, which lets the MPC discuss cuts; a 3.5% level 'is possible' though hard to say what the MPC will decide. Risks: strong 2025 GDP (3.6%), Dec retail/industry, Dec wage acceleration possibly one-off.

PAP: economists see recent MPC decisions and Glapinski's remarks consistent with further small cuts, ideally at projection rounds, possibly to 3.25%. WIIW forecasts Polish public debt at 72% of GDP in 2028. Eurostat: Polish retail sales Dec +4.0% y/y, +0.6% m/m.
